---
name: Update PR Description
description: >-
  Regenerates a PR title and description on `/update-pr`. A pre-agent step
  gathers the PR metadata, commits, a noise-filtered diff, and the mnemonic
  notes at the head SHA into /tmp/gh-aw/pr-context/; the agent only reads those
  files and emits one update_pull_request safe output. Supports a staged
  dry-run via workflow_dispatch.

on:
  slash_command:
    name: update-pr
    events: [pull_request_comment]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: PR number to update (required for manual runs)
        required: false
        type: string
      dry_run:
        description: Preview the generated title/description without applying it
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  roles: [admin, maintainer, write]
  reaction: eyes
  status-comment: true

concurrency:
  group: update-pr-description-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.pr_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
  job-discriminator: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.pr_number }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  issues: read
  copilot-requests: write

engine: copilot

timeout-minutes: 10

network:
  allowed:
    - defaults
    - github

tools:
  github:
    toolsets: [repos, pull_requests, issues]
  bash:
    - "cat *"
    - "head *"
    - "tail *"
    - "wc *"
    - "ls *"
    - "grep *"
    - "sed *"
    - "jq *"
    - "sort *"
    - "uniq *"
    - "echo *"
    - "printf *"

steps:
  - name: Gather PR context
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.pr_number }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      : "${PR_NUMBER:?pr_number is required for manual runs}"
      out=/tmp/gh-aw/pr-context
      mkdir -p "$out/notes"
      repo="$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"

      gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$repo" \
        --json number,url,title,body,author,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid,additions,deletions,changedFiles,labels,closingIssuesReferences \
        > "$out/pr.json"
      head_sha=$(jq -r .headRefOid "$out/pr.json")

      gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/commits" \
        --jq '.[] | "### " + (.sha[0:7]) + " " + (.commit.message | split("\n")[0]) + "\n\n" + (.commit.message | split("\n")[1:] | join("\n") | ltrimstr("\n")) + "\n"' \
        > "$out/commits.md"

      gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files" \
        --jq '.[] | [.status, (.additions|tostring), (.deletions|tostring), .filename] | @tsv' \
        > "$out/files.tsv"

      # gh pr diff refuses very large PRs; fall back to per-file patches.
      if ! gh pr diff "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$repo" > "$out/full.diff" 2>/dev/null; then
        gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files" \
          --jq '.[] | "diff --git a/\(.filename) b/\(.filename)\n\(.patch // "(patch unavailable: binary or too large)")"' \
          > "$out/full.diff"
      fi

      noise='(^|/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock)$|\.lock\.yml$|^\.mnemonic/|^dist/|\.snap$|^\.github/aw/actions-lock\.json$'
      awk -v noise="$noise" '
        /^diff --git / { path = $3; sub(/^a\//, "", path); skip = (path ~ noise) }
        !skip
      ' "$out/full.diff" > "$out/diff.patch"

      awk -F'\t' '$4 ~ /^\.mnemonic\/notes\/.*\.md$/ && $1 != "removed" { print $4 }' "$out/files.tsv" |
        while IFS= read -r note; do
          gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" "repos/$repo/contents/$note?ref=$head_sha" \
            > "$out/notes/$(basename "$note")" || rm -f "$out/notes/$(basename "$note")"
        done

      {
        echo "files changed: $(wc -l < "$out/files.tsv")"
        echo "diff.patch lines (noise filtered): $(wc -l < "$out/diff.patch")"
        echo "commits: $(grep -c '^### ' "$out/commits.md" || true)"
        echo "notes: $(find "$out/notes" -type f | wc -l)"
      } | tee "$out/stats.txt"

safe-outputs:
  update-pull-request:
    target: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr_number || github.event.issue.number }}
    title: true
    body: true
    operation: replace
    staged: ${{ github.event.inputs.dry_run == 'true' }}
  messages:
    footer: "> Generated by [{workflow_name}]({run_url}) from the diff, commits, and `.mnemonic/notes/`. Comment `/update-pr` to regenerate."

---
# Write the title and description for PR #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.pr_number }}

You are a senior engineer on ${{ github.repository }}, writing the description a reviewer reads before opening the diff. It has to tell them what changed, why, and where to look closely.

## Inputs

Everything you need is already on disk in `/tmp/gh-aw/pr-context/`. Start with `cat /tmp/gh-aw/pr-context/stats.txt`, then read:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `pr.json` | Current title, body, author, branches, labels, `closingIssuesReferences` |
| `commits.md` | Every commit message, oldest first |
| `files.tsv` | `status  additions  deletions  path` for every changed file (including lock files and notes) |
| `diff.patch` | The unified diff, without lock files, compiled `.lock.yml` workflows, `dist/`, snapshots, and `.mnemonic/` |
| `notes/*.md` | The mnemonic notes added or modified in this PR, at the PR head |

Page through `diff.patch` with `sed -n 'START,ENDp'` when it's long. Read all of it for PRs under ~3000 lines. For larger PRs, read every hunk under `src/`, then skim tests and the rest. The GitHub MCP tools are read-only extras (for example, a linked issue body or a full file at the head SHA). Don't use `gh`; it's not authenticated here.

### What the notes are

`.mnemonic/notes/` holds the author's design memory. Each note has YAML frontmatter (`title`, `tags`, `role`, `lifecycle`) and a markdown body.

- **Permanent notes** (no `role`, or `lifecycle: permanent`) record decisions and rationale: why this approach, which alternatives were rejected, constraints, tradeoffs. They're your main source for the "why".
- **Workflow notes** (`role: research | plan | review | context`, or `lifecycle: temporary`, including titles starting with `Research:`, `Plan:`, `Review:`, `Apply:`, `Checkpoint:`, `RPIR request:`) are process artifacts. Mine them for facts: the problem statement, verified claims, review findings, test evidence. Don't let them shape the structure, and never use their titles as the PR title.

Notes are optional. Many PRs have none, and the diff and commits are enough.

## Title

- Imperative mood, present tense: "Add …", "Fix …", "Make … configurable".
- Name the user-visible or architectural change, not the process ("Apply: …", "Implement plan …").
- 72 characters max. No trailing period, no conventional-commit prefix unless the current title already uses one.

## Body

Use these sections in this order. Leave a section out when you'd have to pad it.

```markdown
## Summary

2–4 sentences: what changes for users or maintainers, and why it was needed.

## Changes

- Bullets grouped by behavior or component, not by file. Name the important
  functions, config keys, env vars, CLI flags, or MCP tools involved (`backticks`).
  Mention a file only when it helps the reviewer find something.

## Design decisions

- The key choices and their reasons: alternatives considered, constraints,
  tradeoffs, things deliberately left out. Mostly from permanent notes and commit
  bodies. Omit this section when nothing was decided beyond the obvious.

## Compatibility and risk

- Breaking changes, migrations, changed defaults, new config, re-index or
  re-embed requirements, performance impact. Omit when there are none.

## Testing

- What the tests cover (new or changed test files, and what they assert) and any
  verification or review results recorded in the notes.

## Related

- `Fixes #N` / `Closes #N` lines carried over from the current body or `closingIssuesReferences`.
- <details><summary>Mnemonic notes (N)</summary> one line per note:
  `` `path` — title `` marking workflow notes with their role </details>
```

## Quality bar

- Every statement must be backed by the diff, a commit message, or a note. If the notes and the diff disagree, trust the diff.
- Be concrete: "Chunks are capped at `EMBED_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS` (default 4000)" beats "Improves chunking".
- No filler ("various improvements", "several changes", "this PR updates some files"), no marketing tone, no file-by-file dump.
- Keep a hand-written paragraph from the current body only if it adds information the diff can't provide, such as motivation or a screenshot link. Drop previously generated text.
- Aim for a description a reviewer can read in under two minutes.

## Emit the result

1. Write the body with the file creation tool to `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr_body.md`.
2. Submit title and body in a single command:

   ```bash
   jq -n --arg title "YOUR TITLE" --rawfile body /tmp/gh-aw/agent/pr_body.md '{title: $title, body: $body}' | safeoutputs update_pull_request .
   ```

`update_pull_request` can be called **once**. Don't probe it or send placeholder content. If the command fails, fix the payload (don't change the approach) and retry at most twice, then call `report_incomplete` with the error.

Call `noop` instead only when the PR has no changed files, or when your title and body match `pr.json` exactly.

Don't edit repository files, post comments, or open issues.
